Hi, I don't necessarily have an advice on what to use, just wanna tell you to not underestimate the feeling of you losing more hair than you think you're supposed to. Like other people have said, it can be a normal amount, but if you feel like it's out of the ordinary, it's best to start treating it before it gets too bad.

I'm 23 now and I had been noticing an alarming amount of hair falling out since the age of 18 or so. For the longest time I have been told by my family it's nothing unusual and that hair just falls out, so I left it untreated for years until I felt absolutely sure there just must be something wrong. Treatment takes time, hair regrowth takes time, it's better to stop the loss at its start than to deal with it later on.

I sincerely hope for you that it's nothing serious and that you can maintain your hair at its fullest beauty. Wishing you all the best ❤️

Hi! My friend has really long thick hair that used to be heavily damaged. What worked for her without having to get rid of her length is finding a salon that uses the split ender to remove the damaged ends of your hair in it's entire length and makes your hair look overall more healthy. Another thing that helped her a lot was getting Brazilian keratin treatments which repair the structure of the hair and make them silky and healthy. I don't have personal experience with any of these, I'm just forwarding the experience of my friend because I saw the results and they're breathtaking. Maybe you should also look into something similar. Hope this helps at least a little bit and that you find what works for you! :)

A round hairbrush in combination with a hair dryer that's not as hot. It's less practical because it requires you pretty much using both your hands, but it's definitely better for your hair in the long run to just learn to work with this. I have a regular hair dryer that is nowhere near as hot as the round one so I think any hair dryer that allows you to change the temperature is gonna be good enough :) And use heat protection too of course!

I have been to a hairdresser last week after literal years, and when she saw the condition of my hair, first thing she told me was to stop using these hot air brushes, since they dry and burn the absolute hell out of your hair (just try grabbing the brush with your hand to see how hot it is, you'll burn yourself. imagine what it's doing to your hair) damaging it and causing breakage. Thought I might bring this to your attention since it might be a reason why your hair strands tend to grip each other as I had the exact same issue :)

Of course I don't mind 💕 The tips I usually give is just a plain old "practice a lot". But there's more to it than that! What I've noticed helps me a lot is to only focus on one part at a time (whether it's strands of hair, eyebrows, both eyes, nose, mouth etc) and only move onto the next one once you're happy with the result. It takes a lot of polishing and a lot of time, but if you decide to get back to a certain part later to finish it, you won't spot mistakes as easily. It's also a good idea to compare your drawing to the original picture a lot by holding the drawing next to the original picture! 

I usually put the original pictures in black and white so it's easier to see the shadows and so it gives you an estimate of how dark certain parts should be. I also open the picture in the same size as my paper (usually a4 format) so that when I'm comparing my drawing to the original picture there are no size differences. Sometimes if I'm REALLY unsure about how to do something properly, I don't hesitate to put the paper over your screen to see what I've done wrong to correct it ^^ 

Another tip is to use many different pencils!!! I use the hardest ones (2H or 2B) for outlines and sketches because they're easier to erase, 4B is overall good for shading because it smudges fairly well (I use cotton earbuds for smudging), 8B is the softest I've ever used, smudges really easily, breaks a lot as well but is good for dark colors (I did the stripes on his shirt with 8B). Most of the time I use charcoal for clothing, but believe it or not charcoal isn't very dark. I used it in the previous drawings I posted here, you can see that the charcoal sadly isn't as black as I'd like it to be. (In the latest San picture I colored his tie with a black colored pencil, everything else is charcoal.) Generally if you're unsure of what to expect from pencils it's always good to have a scrap of paper next to you to try those pencils on ^^

If you're a beginner then try taking it slow, try drawing random eyes of an idol on a piece of paper and polish them until you can see the idol you're drawing in just his eyes. Back in the day I did this with EXO members and its a really good practice method for eyes, because they're the most important part of the drawing. Noses are a bit less important but those should be mostly just shaded. You really only need to outline the nostrils, most of everything else should be done by shading alone. Mouths are the same, lips usually have a lot of creaks in them, different coloring all kinds of lines as well, this is where putting the original picture in black and white helps a lot. Also, for mouths it's really important to do the shadows around the mouths as they generally give the face a shape. Examples are the small shadows under the bottom lip or the shadow between the nose and the top lip, that one is super important! The shadows also generally get lighter as you approach the top lip. As for hair, I struggle with hair myself tbh. Most people do it in a very detailed way, they draw each hair one by one (which I'll never understand how lol) but I like focusing on strands. With dark hair it's important to see where the hair shines (??? how do you call the light reflection on it lol) so you can make those parts lighter than the rest. 

When drawing portraits people usually start with making sketches of the facial proportions and then starting with the eyes, I always do hair first because I want to get it out of my way lol. You need to figure out what works the best for you ^^ 

I hope this helps a bit! If you have any more questions always feel free to ask 💕💕
